_comment: kaizen :: standards catalog index. The catalog is versioned INDEPENDENTLY of the plugin (see docs/decisions/0005-standards-as-versioned-data.md) so practices can ship without a plugin release. Calendar versioning, because freshness is the point.
_surfaces_comment: Where a rule can be rendered. A template marks the spot with <!-- KAIZEN_STANDARDS:<surface> --> and /kaizen:init fills it with the rules that apply to the detected project. Adding a surface means adding it here AND placing the marker in a template — the harness checks both directions.

claude_md.conventions.description: Rules Claude should follow while writing code in this project.

claude_md.never.description: Hard prohibitions. Phrased as things not to do.

rules_testing.conventions.description: Path-scoped rules loaded only when Claude edits test files.

_severity_comment: severity drives how a violation is reported by /kaizen:analyze — it does NOT mean a rule is more or less optional.

severity_levels.security: A violation can lead to a vulnerability. Always reported first.
severity_levels.safety: A violation risks data loss, broken builds, or unrecoverable state.
severity_levels.convention: A violation is inconsistency, not damage. Style and maintainability.

_status_comment: A rule is never deleted from the catalog — it is deprecated, so a project pinned to an older standards version can still explain where its rule came from.
_refines_comment: A stack-specific rule may declare `refines: <ID>` pointing at a general rule that says the same thing less precisely. When both would render into the same project, the general one is suppressed and the specific one wins — a project should be told 'throw Error subclasses', not that plus 'throw domain-specific error types'. The general rule still exists for stacks with no specialisation.
_check_comment: How /kaizen:analyze verifies a rule. A rule with no check is reported under 'Unchecked (manual review)' — explicitly, never silently.

check_types.grep: Regex over include/exclude globs. A match is a violation.
check_types.sibling_file: For each file matching include, a sibling matching pattern must exist.
check_types.none: Not mechanically verifiable. Surfaced as unchecked.
